models.title: Units-of-production depreciation expense
models.summary: Units-of-production depreciation allocates the depreciable cost in proportion to period output.

relationship.original_equation: Depreciation = (cost - residual value) × period production / estimated lifetime production
relationship.translation_notes: Physical output units are identical counts, and their quotient is dimensionless; the result is a currency amount for the reporting period.

models.title: Estimated depreciable-asset age
models.summary: Estimated depreciable-asset age is estimated from accumulated depreciation and annual depreciation.

relationship.original_equation: Estimated depreciable-asset age = accumulated depreciation / annual depreciation
relationship.locator: Printed p142, Equation 5:2 and adjacent age formula
relationship.translation_notes: Annual periods are dimensionless financial counts, not physical seconds. The accessible dissertation gives total life and age from gross cost and book value; the stated balance ratio is the corresponding algebraic proxy.

variables.definition: Estimated number of annual reporting periods for Estimated depreciable-asset age
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: The ratio uses the historical cost model and consistent asset scope and annual accounting periods.
The simple single-asset interpretation assumes straight-line depreciation, stable estimates and zero residual value.
limitations: The numerical proxy is not a verified actual purchase age.
For mixed asset pools, fully depreciated assets, revaluations or impairments, the ratio is only a rough proxy.
